## A third carrier of the superseded boundary, measured — and it is not a spelling

This card's title names **three** 事实层 = `references/` spellings. PR #19379 repairs two of them (`landing-operations.md:27-28` and the `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` "THIRD leg" header). This comment records a third carrier that the `references/` grep does **not** find, because it carries the superseded regime as *missing logic* rather than as stale prose.

### `check-half-states.mjs`'s H43 row is tier-blind

Measured at 2026-09-20T14:58Z on `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`, over the H43 region (the span that builds the row, lines 9940–10110):

| pattern | hits | exit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tier` / `Tier` / `governedTierFor` / `landingTier` | **0** | 1 |
| `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` (firing control, same span) | **5** | 0 |

So H43 decides "this governed PR has asked NOBODY" from `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` alone and never consults the landing tier. Its remedy text prescribes obtaining an authorized approval or using the assign fallback, and its rationale states 「nothing can ship through this gap (the queue guard still refuses an unapproved governed enqueue)」.

Both of those are Tier H statements applied to every governed PR.

### It fires wrongly right now, on the PR fixing the other two carriers

H43 fires on **#19379** — 「open and GOVERNED (1 changed file(s) on the register: `.claude/**`×1), and has asked NOBODY — none of the 2 account(s) in `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` (`os-zhuang`, `hotlong`) is requested, assigned, or has submitted a review」.

But #19379 is **Tier S**, measured with the register's own predicate on its final file list: `.claude/**` hits the `claude-tree` row, whose `tier` is `GOVERNED_TIER_S`; `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` is not a registered surface. And the Tier S landing rule, in the predicate's own words, says the opposite of H43's remedy:

> the OWNING seat lands this PR through the queue once its thread (or its card) carries a `## Contract review` record for the CURRENT head […] ⛔ **no seat approves it either, and no maintainer click is waited for.**

The rationale limb is falsified too: the queue guard does **not** refuse a Tier S enqueue. PR #19351 (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` + two `references/` files + a `scripts/pm/` script, **0 reviews**) had `Governed Surface Guard` complete `success` on its queue build at 2026-09-20T14:03:11Z and merged as `231283a6e2` at 2026-09-20T14:28:02Z — on a review of record, exactly as the tier prescribes.

### Why this one is worth fixing even though H43 blocks nothing

H43 is report-only, so no PR is held by it. The cost is that a seat that follows its remedy asks `os-zhuang` or `hotlong` to look at a pull request the regime does not require them to look at — which is the precise burden the 2026-09-18 tiering (#19133, 「同意改规则。」, amended 「我觉得这些我也没必要确认」) was ruled to remove. An instrument that keeps asking for the click the ruling abolished re-imposes it by habit.

⛔ Not filed as a separate card and ⛔ no label written: this belongs to this card's own "three spellings" family, and it is the taker's call whether it rides #19379 or a follow-up. ⛔ This seat is not claiming this card and asserts nothing about its priority.

**Suggested shape of the repair, for the taker to accept or reject:** H43 already has the register imported for `GOVERNED_SURFACES`; reading `governedTierFor` on the same paths it already matched would let the row stand down on Tier S entirely, or — if a Tier S PR with no review of record is still worth surfacing — fire with the Tier S remedy (post the at-tier `## Contract review` record) instead of the approval one. ⛔ Whether to narrow or to re-aim is a judgement this comment does not make.

## Handback — the at-tier review of PR #19379 returned FAIL, 2026-09-20T18:07Z

Record: PR #19379 comment [`5751616940`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/19379#issuecomment-5751616940), head `fa628d0b3602a4df059add483084b23b826c85f9`, **VERDICT: FAIL**. Adopted verbatim by `domain:spec` seat 4; ⛔ not rewritten. Shape verified against GitHub: all nine required lines, `Served-tier` the constant name, `Head-sha` in a span of its own matching the head, zero angle brackets.

| line | value | kind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Implemented-by:` | `claude/pm-superseded-references-tier` | branch — `mode:subagent` |
| `Reviewed-by:` | `session_01AmH9bKvGoLjiY86Q4Z3og2` | the adopting seat |

**Carriers:** neither PR #19379 nor this card carries `needs:contract-review`, so there was nothing to strip and nothing was written. Card state (`pm:queue`) and assignee (none) untouched.

### Two defects, both inside the PR's own scope, both one line

1. `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md:27` — the new 「Tier S(`.claude/**` 全树)者」 names the **surface** and drops the PR-level ALL quantifier that its predecessor (「受管路径全在…者」), this card's prescribed wording, and sibling `contract-review.md:46` all carry. Lines 27/28 now partition surfaces rather than pull requests, so a mixed diff matches two lines with no tiebreak on the page. The quantified form measures 105 B against a 120 B cap.
2. `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs:4442-4443` — the `--self-test` SUCCESS line, printed on every run, still says 「the #18020 references TIER: a governed diff whose governed paths all lie under the one ruled prefix lands on the skills seat's review of record」, while the battery at `:3949-3950` asserts `the-old-references-boundary-is-GONE`. The PR claims to have removed this file's self-contradiction; this instance is still live.

### Ruling on H43 — the PR is NOT incomplete for lacking it

The reviewer verified the third-carrier claim independently and ruled that leaving H43 to this card is **correct**: it is missing logic rather than stale prose (a lazy `governedTierFor` import in a file that travels to sibling repos, plus a `check:pm-half-states` self-test case), i.e. a behaviour change in a non-governed instrument, which does not belong under a docs-only Tier S record. It rides with **H48** (`:11304-11509`), tier-blind by the same instrument, in one half-states PR.

Two obligations it names: this card's **body** should enumerate H43 as an item — today it exists only in a comment — and the PR's "On the card" paragraph should list H43 among the untouched items.

Its own span reading corrects mine: at this head the H43 row spans `check-half-states.mjs:10023-10259`, not the ≈9940-10110 I measured. Its anchored counts over the true span agree with the substance — `tier`/`Tier`/`governedTierFor`/`landingTier`/`GOVERNED_TIER_[HS]` all **0**, `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` **5** — with a radius control over the whole 36,335-line file (`tier` 83, `Tier` 55, `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` 7) and the sharper fact that `governedTierFor` is **0 in the entire file: it is never imported**.

### Still stating the superseded boundary after this PR

Live: `.claude/agents/os-dev.md:286-287` · `SKILL.md:608` 「⛔ 无事实层例外」 (vocabulary) · the queue-guard `:4442-4443` above. Naming-only uses of "the references tier" as the leg's name are optional tidy, and several sites citing the old boundary **as history** are correct as they stand.

### Two errors of this seat, both measured, both named

1. **An identifier this seat never read.** The comment recording the third carrier was cited as `5750553107`. Measured: that id returns **HTTP 404**. The real one is **`5750573385`** (this card, 2026-09-20T14:58:09Z). The cause is not a transcription slip — when posting it this seat printed only the tail of the tool's output and never saw the `comment:` line at all, then stated an id anyway, and carried it into the review brief and into the maintainer report. ⛔ An identifier that was not read is not a reading.
2. **Work dispatched on a card this seat never claimed.** `--pair 19379` reads exit 4 on **C2**: no `Claim:` on this card names `claude/pm-superseded-references-tier`, and the PR body carries no `Clause-②` line. This card is `domain:skills`; `domain:spec` seat 4 opened a PR against it without claiming it, which is the root of that refusal and not a defect in the diff. ⛔ This seat is not claiming the card now to paper over it — the claim belongs to whichever seat takes the rework, and that seat must post it with `Clause-②: no` before any PASS record can bring `--pair` to 0.

## ⚠️ A cross-lane claim, stated rather than quietly taken

This card is `domain:skills`. This seat is `domain:spec` seat 4. The claim is posted on the maintainer's explicit instruction to follow up on PR #19379, and it is written here so the record shows **why** a spec seat holds a skills card rather than leaving a reader to infer it.

The card has been `pm:queue` with **no assignee and no `Claim:` from anyone** since it was filed on 2026-09-18T23:15:58Z; the skills seat's only act on it is a scope addendum (`5737973707`, 2026-09-19T00:47:02Z). ⛔ If the skills seat wants it back, this claim is retracted on request — a `Release:` costs one comment and this seat will write it.

## What this claim repairs, and what it does not

`check-clause2-carriers --pair 19379` reads exit 4 on **C2**: no claim on this card names `claude/pm-superseded-references-tier`, and the PR body carries no `Clause-②` line. ⛔ That refusal is this seat's own doing — it opened PR #19379 against an unclaimed card in another lane, which is the root of C2 and not a defect in the diff. Recorded on the PR and on this card already; the claim above is the repair.

`Clause-②: no` — the PR's surface is `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md` and `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`. The register answers **Tier S** on that file list (the `.claude/**` row; the guard script is not a registered surface), so ⛔ no seat approves it and no maintainer click is owed — it lands on the at-tier contract review record. ⛔ Routing, not a ruling.

## The rework this claim covers

The at-tier review `5751616940` (head `fa628d0b36`) returned **FAIL** on two one-line defects:

1. `landing-operations.md:27` — the new 「Tier S(`.claude/**` 全树)者」 drops the PR-level ALL quantifier that its predecessor, this card's prescribed wording and sibling `contract-review.md:46` all carry, so lines 27/28 now partition **surfaces** rather than **pull requests** and a mixed diff matches two lines with no tiebreak.
2. `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs:4442-4443` — the `--self-test` SUCCESS line, printed every run, still states the superseded #18020 references-tier boundary while the battery at `:3949-3950` asserts it is GONE.

Also carried, from the same review: this card's **body** should enumerate **H43** as an item (today it exists only in comment `5750573385`), and PR #19379's "On the card" paragraph should list H43 among the untouched items. The review ruled the PR **not incomplete** for leaving H43 to this card — it is missing logic in a non-governed instrument and rides with **H48** in a half-states PR, not under a docs-only Tier S record.

Dispatching the rework now.

## Handback — round 2 FAIL, and it overturns this seat's own framing of the blocker, 2026-09-21T02:20Z

Record: PR #19379 comment [`5754554617`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/19379#issuecomment-5754554617), head `71216fcff6d2cd314784ce7746ccd91095751ea7`, **VERDICT: FAIL**. Adopted verbatim; ⛔ not rewritten.

### ⛔ The seat reported the blocker backwards, and the record corrects it

This seat told the maintainer that `--pair 19379`'s exit 2 made the Tier S landing predicate **unsatisfiable**, that a rename would **strand** the review record anchored to this branch, and that the live options were A (land over a declared exit 2) or B (widen `CLAIM_BRANCH_SHAPE`). **All three of those are wrong**, and the load-bearing facts were in the repo the whole time:

- `AGENTS.md:460` — 「**Name the branch after the issue it fixes: `claude/issue-<n>-<slug>`.**」
- `AGENTS.md:395` — the claim carries 「the session ID and the branch (`claude/issue-<n>-<slug>`)」

So the branch-name shape **is the contract**, and `CLAIM_BRANCH_SHAPE` is that contract made mechanical. The predicate is not unsatisfiable — **this branch is non-conforming**. `claude/pm-superseded-references-tier` violates `AGENTS.md:460`, and it has since the round-1 implementer named it.

Therefore, per the record:
- **Option A is a seat overriding Prime Directive #14** (which reads 「Tier S by the owning seat on a contract-tier review of record; before that record no AI seat merges, reads 0 and every check is green」 and ends 「No seat judges this」). Ruled out.
- **Option B — widening the shape — is a PD #5 workaround.** Ruled out.
- **Option C is the repair, and a rename does NOT strand anything**: GitHub keeps the PR, its thread, its head and its comments. What is owed is one **new `Claim:` naming a conforming branch** and a **fresh record** whose `Implemented-by:` names it, at the repaired head.

⚠️ The implementer's class-(b) finding against the checker and PD #14 is **mis-aimed**, and this seat amplified it to the maintainer rather than checking `AGENTS.md`. ⛔ Recorded as the seat's error, not the implementer's alone: the seat had the means to read `:460` and did not.

### The FAIL defect itself — one word, and neither earlier artefact has it

`scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs:4444` — the re-keyed `--self-test` SUCCESS line still says Tier S 「lands on the **skills seat's** review of record」. That is the **pre-#19133 actor**. PD #14 (`AGENTS.md:255-256`, `:275`), the register (`check-governed-merges.mjs:316/:1015/:1559`), the queue guard's own printed verdicts (`:1426`, `:1489`), `SKILL.md:522/:609` and `contract-review.md:26` all say the **owning** seat. **This very PR is the counter-example** — Tier S, landing on `domain:spec` seat 4's records.
